title: Al-Muhyi, the Giver of Life
tomorrow: if life is His, what do Muslims say when someone dies?

lines: A SEED IN A PAPER CUP.
cards: A seed in a paper cup on a classroom windowsill. You water it, and nothing. Water it, nothing.
Then one morning there's a green hook pushing up through the dirt, and the whole class crowds around. Abraham wants to see something like that, only far bigger.
In Surah al-Baqarah he says, in Pickthall's words: "My Lord! Show me how Thou givest life to the dead." And God answers with a question of His own: "Dost thou not believe?"

teach.h: SO MY HEART MAY BE AT EASE.
teach.b: Abraham's answer is a very human line: "Yea, but (I ask) in order that my heart may be at ease." He believes. He just wants his heart to catch up with what he believes.
And he isn't scolded. He's given something to do.
Take four birds, the verse says, and tame them to yourself. Then set a part of them on each hill, and call them, and they will come to you in haste.
Some readers notice the taming: Abraham has to know these birds first, so that when they come flying back, he'll know they're the same ones. Today's Name is Al-Muhyi, the Giver of Life.
And the Qur'an keeps a smaller picture of it in plain view.
In Surah ar-Rum: "Look, therefore, at the prints of Allah's mercy (in creation): how He quickeneth the earth after her death."
To quicken is old English for to make alive, not to speed up.
Dry, cracked ground, then rain, then green.
Here's the thing to tell a friend tonight: in the Qur'an, a prophet asks for proof so his heart can rest, and the answer is a hands-on lesson with birds he had to get to know first.

how: Muslims call on Allah as Al-Muhyi, the Giver of Life, and the Qur'an's verses of rain reviving dead earth are recited as signs of His power to give life again.

o: the Giver of Life, to earth and to the dead
the Creator who made the first life only
the Healer who cures every illness

games.q: the story and the sign — tap the pairs.
p: asked to see life given to the dead
quickens the earth after her death

s: Abraham was scolded for asking to see how the dead are given life
he said he asked so his heart would be at ease, and he was given the birds.
the Qur'an uses rain on dead earth as a picture of life given
"how He quickeneth the earth after her death."
to quicken is old English for to make alive. Al-Muhyi gives life.

games.q: your friend believes, but before a big surgery he says, 'i want to SEE that it'll be ok.' someone tells him that's weak faith. what does Abraham's story say?
o: they're right; real faith never asks for anything.
asking so the heart can be at ease is in the Qur'an, from Abraham.
he should stop believing until he gets his proof.
games.why: Abraham believed and still asked, 'that my heart may be at ease.' he wasn't scolded; he was given the birds.

practice: If there's a plant near you, touch the soil to see if it's dry, and water it slowly if it is. If there's a pet, sit with it.
If neither, look out a window at one living thing, a tree, a bird, grass pushing through pavement, and keep it company for the two minutes.

wordCard.voice: Al-Muhyi. The Giver of Life: to dead ground after rain, to four birds on four hills, and to the dead.

orig.note: Arabic: the Giver of Life. in Surah ar-Rum, Pickthall calls Him the Quickener of the Dead.

carryVoice: A line for the road: life is his, in the seedling on the sill and in the one listening. Fifteen thirty-four, done.
